beats.label: S1 · The card
beats.text: Gi-hun, a broke gambler estranged from his daughter, takes a stranger's card after a subway ddakji game and wakes in a dorm with 455 other debtors.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Gi-hun's debt-driven consent and the recruiter as the games' only known thread to the outside world.

beats.label: S1 · Red Light
beats.text: The first game turns lethal; Gi-hun survives and allies with Sang-woo, elderly Il-nam, migrant Ali, and pickpocket Sae-byeok.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the five relationships that will define every moral choice Gi-hun makes for the rest of the run.

beats.label: S1 · Vote and return
beats.text: The players vote to end the games and go home, but debt drags almost everyone back — the games run on consent, not capture.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the vote mechanic that becomes central to season 2 and frames Gi-hun's later crusade as an argument, not a rescue.

beats.label: S1 · The infiltrator
beats.text: Detective Jun-ho slips in disguised as a pink guard, discovers the games have run 30 years, and finds his missing brother won the 2015 iteration.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the brother reveal and gives the outside world one witness who has seen the island from within.

beats.label: S1 · Marbles
beats.text: Gi-hun tricks Il-nam, who lets him win anyway; Sang-woo cons Ali into forfeiting and dies. Winning now means killing your friends.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the moral break Gi-hun never recovers from and the reason he refuses to spend the prize money.

beats.label: S1 · Brother in the mask
beats.text: Sang-woo kills Sae-byeok on the last night. Jun-ho reaches the Front Man, learns he is his brother In-ho, and is shot off a cliff into the sea.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Fixes the season's central antagonist as In-ho and leaves Jun-ho's fate open — both engines of season 2.

beats.label: S1 · Turn back
beats.text: Gi-hun wins after Sang-woo takes his own life; a dying Il-nam admits he built the games for bored VIPs. A year later Gi-hun spots the Recruiter and abandons his flight home.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The choice at the jet bridge is the whole premise of season 2 — Gi-hun stays to end the games instead of seeing his daughter.

cliffhanger.text: Gi-hun has walked away from his flight to his daughter and picked a fight with the Front Man by phone, with no way in besides the Recruiter and no idea Jun-ho survived.
questions: How does Gi-hun reach the games with no address, no ally, and only a phone line?
Did Jun-ho survive the fall into the sea?
What will In-ho do to the man now hunting his operation?

characters.name: Sang-woo
characters.line: Gi-hun's childhood friend, a disgraced investment banker on the run for embezzlement who becomes ruthless in the games, betrays Ali, murders Sae-byeok, and takes his own life in the final round.

characters.name: Sae-byeok
characters.line: A North Korean defector and pickpocket playing to buy her mother out of the North and rescue her younger brother, killed by Sang-woo on the final night.

characters.name: Ali
characters.line: A Pakistani migrant worker owed unpaid wages who befriends Gi-hun's group, conned out of his marbles by Sang-woo and eliminated.

characters.name: Jun-ho
characters.line: A detective who infiltrates the island disguised as a pink guard searching for his missing brother, only to discover the Front Man is that brother In-ho, who shoots him off a cliff into the sea.

characters.name: The Recruiter
characters.line: The sharp-suited salesman who lures debtors into the games via ddakji in subway stations, spotted by Gi-hun again a year after his win.

beats.label: S2 · Two years later
beats.text: Gi-hun runs a hotel-fort operation with ex-loan sharks to hunt the Recruiter, while Jun-ho, secretly alive, searches for the island by boat with Captain Park.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resets both hunts and introduces Park, the mole who will quietly undo Jun-ho's search from underneath him.

beats.label: S2 · Roulette and surrender
beats.text: They corner the Recruiter, who forces Gi-hun into Russian roulette and dies — the only outside thread is severed, so Gi-hun surrenders himself as a player wearing a tracker.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why Gi-hun is back inside the arena at all and why his outside team is now blind and searching for a signal.

beats.label: S2 · Two moles
beats.text: In-ho enters the dorm as Player 001, feigning friendship with Gi-hun to steer him from within; on the water, Captain Park is quietly In-ho's man.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's core betrayal architecture — everyone Gi-hun and Jun-ho trust most is In-ho — and it's still hidden at season's end.

beats.label: S2 · The vote rule
beats.text: A new rule lets players vote after each round to end the games. Gi-hun reveals he is a former winner and pleads to stop; In-ho's swing vote keeps them running.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Makes Gi-hun's crusade a political one — he has to persuade a majority — and hands In-ho the mechanism to sabotage him from inside.

beats.label: S2 · No-eul in pink
beats.text: North Korean defector Kang No-eul joins the pink guards to earn her daughter's rescue, then starts mercy-killing wounded players to sabotage the guards' organ-harvesting racket.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Opens a second front inside the facility — a guard actively working against the operation, with her own hostage-daughter clock.

beats.label: S2 · The uprising
beats.text: After Mingle, Gi-hun convinces the losing-vote players to seize the guards' guns and march on the control room. Half his allies die on the way as ammunition runs out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's active choice — Gi-hun stops arguing and starts a war — and it fails in real time, leaving him captured.

beats.label: S2 · Mask back on
beats.text: In-ho fakes his death mid-battle, puts the Front Man's mask back on, and executes Gi-hun's oldest friend Jung-bae in front of him while Park sabotages Jun-ho's approach from the sea.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is where season 2 ends: the rebellion crushed, In-ho openly against Gi-hun, and Jun-ho still trusting his own captor.

cliffhanger.text: Gi-hun's uprising has collapsed with his allies dead around him and the Front Man's mask back on. Jun-ho is closer to the island than ever, still unaware his captain works for his brother.
questions: What is left of Gi-hun after being forced to watch Jung-bae die at In-ho's hand?
How long before Jun-ho sees through Captain Park?
Can any of the surviving players hold together now that In-ho is openly hunting them?

characters.name: Captain Park
characters.line: The boat captain Jun-ho hires to hunt the island, secretly loyal to the Front Man and sabotaging the search from within.

characters.name: Kang No-eul
characters.line: A North Korean defector who takes a job as a pink guard to earn her daughter's rescue, then begins mercy-killing wounded players to disrupt the guards' organ-harvesting side racket.

characters.name: The Recruiter
characters.line: The salesman Gi-hun hunts down; cornered, he forces Gi-hun into a game of Russian roulette and dies, severing Gi-hun's only lead to the games from the outside.

characters.name: Jun-ho
characters.line: The detective, secretly alive after being shot off the cliff, circling the archipelago by boat with Captain Park in search of the island, unaware his guide answers to his brother.
